compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Intel Arc B580 Xe2: SIMD16 typical, supports wave intrinsics, fp16 packed math. cs_6_8 with 32KiB groupshared cap. Compute-light: 16*9=144 MACs/output * 7.37M outputs ≈ 1.06 GMAC, mostly bandwidth-bound.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Conv 3x3, IC=16, OC=32 fused with ReLU + 2x2 avgpool. Output 1x32x360x640. Weights tiny (4608 fp16 = 9KB), fits in groupshared as compact reusable read-only tile. Activation quantizer is identity here (quantize=False), so it's just conv -> ReLU -> avgpool.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input: 14.7M fp16 (~29MB). Output: 7.37M fp16 (~14.7MB). Weights: 9KB (cacheable). Bandwidth-bound likely.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Padded boundary handling; ensure coalesced reads.

register_pressure.notes: Per-thread: if one thread computes one 2x2 pooled output (=4 conv outputs at one OC), needs 4 accumulators + tile of inputs. Manageable.

nodes.notes:
ANALYSIS:
1) Classification: fused Conv2D(3x3, IC=16, OC=32, stride=1, pad=1) + ReLU + AvgPool2d(2). Activation quantizer disabled (quantize=False -> identity passthrough). Dense, no reductions across blocks; per-output reduction over 16*3*3=144 MACs. Then 2x2 avg.
2) Math: y[oc,oh,ow] = ReLU(bias[oc] + sum_{ic,kh,kw} w[oc,ic,kh,kw] * x[ic, 2*oh + kh - 1 + dh, 2*ow + kw - 1 + dw]) averaged over 2x2 pool window. Actually pool comes after activation. Output[oc, ph, pw] = avg over 2x2 of ReLU(conv at (2ph+i, 2pw+j)). Pool stride=2 default.
3) Layout: NCHW contiguous. Input (1,16,720,1280). Output (1,32,360,640). Weights (32,16,3,3) tiny - perfect for groupshared read-only tile loaded once per group. Bias 32 floats.
4) Regimes: (a) BW-bound dominant: input streaming. (b) Weight reuse via shared: weights 9KB loaded once. (c) Boundary handling regime around image edges.
5) Knobs: tile shape (output pooled-pixels per group), threads per group, weights in groupshared vs registers, input tile shared vs streamed, OC partition across threads/waves, fp16 packed math, vector load widths.
6) Skeleton: one threadgroup processes a tile of pooled output (e.g., 8x16 pooled = 16x32 conv outputs needing 18x34 input rows for 3x3). Load weights once into groupshared. Each thread computes some output pixels accumulating in registers; uses ReLU then 2x2 averages either via wave intrinsics or shared.
7) Families:
   F1 (TOP) Full fusion, weights in groupshared, threadgroup-tiled output with input tile in groupshared: best reuse, single dispatch.
   F2 Full fusion, weights in registers (broadcast via WaveReadLaneAt) per-thread one pooled pixel, stream inputs from SRV with L2 reuse.
   F3 Channel-parallel: each wave handles all 32 OCs for one spatial tile, leveraging wave intrinsics.
Full fusion is feasible because weights+bias tiny and intermediates fit in registers.

action.description: Single-dispatch fused conv3x3+ReLU+avgpool2x2. Each threadgroup owns a tile of pooled outputs (e.g., 8x8 pooled = 16x16 conv outputs). Load weights (32*16*9=4608 fp16, 9KB) and bias into groupshared once. Load input tile (16ch * 18 * 18 ≈ 10.4KB fp16) into groupshared as reusable read-only tile. Each thread computes one pooled output pixel for one OC (or a small OC vector), accumulating 4 conv positions in registers, applying ReLU, then averaging. Output written directly to UAV.
action.rationale: Weights are reused across all output spatial positions (huge reuse). Input tile reused across OCs and across 2x2 pool window. Both warrant groupshared. Computation per thread stays register-resident.

action.description: Single-dispatch fused kernel where each wave (32 lanes) owns one independent tile (e.g., one pooled row segment for several OCs). Weights loaded into groupshared once for entire threadgroup (multiple waves share). Input streamed from SRV t0 directly into registers with L2 reuse across neighbor lanes. Use WaveReadLaneAt to share input pixels between lanes computing adjacent output positions, reducing redundant SRV reads.

action.title: Increase per-thread output footprint: each thread owns 2x2 pooled (4x4 conv) x fewer OCs, drop THREADS_Z

nodes.notes: CURRENT: does: Each thread owns a 4x4 conv / 2x2 pooled region across all 32 OCs; 4x4 threadgroup, 18x18x16 input tile + full weights+bias staged in LDS. bottleneck: correctness bug (max_diff=7.86e-2). FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent: yes. UPDATE_BELIEF: Implementation likely has an indexing/boundary bug in the 6x6 input window or pool/output write addressing; LDS usage (~21KB weights + ~10KB input) is still under 32KB but the 4x4 thread mapping means each thread does 16 conv outputs * 32 OCs = 512 MACs/IC*9 -- huge register pressure may also be causing spills, but the actual failure is numerical. next bet: Either fix the bug (verify cx0/cy0 indexing and gs_input layout vs declared [IC][IN_TILE_Y][IN_TILE_X]) OR back off to 2x2 conv (1x1 pooled) per thread which is smaller and safer. Prefer a smaller-footprint refinement of n1 rather than chasing this exact mapping. PERF_GAP: expected 1.4x over 31.5x (=~44x); observed: failed correctness.

action.title: Vectorize input loads (ushort2/uint) and pack gs_input as [ty][tx][c] for coalesced register fills

nodes.notes:
CURRENT: does: Repacked gs_input to [ty][tx][c] and attempted vector fp16x2 loads via ByteAddressBuffer, but channels are stride H*W apart in NCHW so the 'vector' loads fell back to two scalar load_fp16 calls each doing an aligned uint load+shift. bottleneck: bandwidth/load-issue still scalar; layout change alone didn't reduce traffic.
FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent: partial. Intent was coalesced vectorized loads; implementation packs gs_input by channel-innermost but loads are still scalar (and likely buggy on odd-aligned indices), causing max_diff=2.67 correctness failure.
UPDATE_BELIEF: Channel-innermost packing in NCHW doesn't enable wide loads since channels are far apart in memory; vectorization needs to be along W (adjacent gx pairs) which then conflicts with [ty][tx][c] packing index by tx. The correctness failure likely stems from boundary/alignment handling in load_fp16 for the halo or from misindexed pairs. Next bet: drop n1b layout change; instead try wide loads along W (consume tx,tx+1 pairs) while keeping gs_input [c][ty][tx] layout, OR try OC tiling refinements that don't touch the input loader.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: Mutually exclusive with n1b (which packed [ty][tx][c] and loaded scalar). Here we keep [c][ty][tx] layout (matches conv inner-loop access) and exploit NCHW W-contiguity by issuing aligned uint loads that pack 2 adjacent gx fp16s, halving address generation and load instructions on the halo loader. Risk: 18-wide row needs odd-end handling; alignment of (gy*W_IN+gx) must be even.

Halves THREADS_Z so each thread accumulates 16 OCs over the same 2x2 conv region, doubling weight reuse per input read and reducing total threadgroups' input-tile loading pressure. Risk: register pressure (4 conv positions x 16 OCs = 64 fp accumulators per thread).

kernel_summary: Fused Conv2D(3x3, IC=16, OC=32, stride=1, pad=1) + ReLU + AvgPool2d(2x2, stride=2) on fp16 NCHW input (1,16,720,1280) producing (1,32,360,640). Activation quantizer is identity since quantize=False. Weights are tiny (4608 fp16 = 9KB) making them an ideal groupshared read-only reusable table; the kernel is memory-bandwidth dominated on input/output streaming. Target Intel Arc B580 (Xe2) using cs_6_8 with 32KiB groupshared cap. Key design pivot is whether to stage the input tile in groupshared (high reuse across OCs and 2x2 pool window) versus streaming through cache, and whether to map one thread per pooled output pixel or use wave intrinsics for cross-lane sharing.
open_questions: Is the activation_quantizer truly an identity passthrough when quantize=False, or does it still apply max_log clamping?
What wave size does the Intel Arc B580 / DXIL path actually use (SIMD16 vs SIMD32) and does [WaveSize(32)] work reliably?
Does fp16 packed-math (mad in fp16) deliver throughput gains, or should we accumulate in fp32 for stability and only cast on store?
Optimal output tile size per threadgroup balancing groupshared (weights + halo input) vs occupancy?
Are typed Buffer<float16_t> loads coalesced enough or should we use ByteAddressBuffer with packed uint loads (two fp16 per uint)?
How costly is the boundary padding branch — should the kernel split into interior fast path and border path?
Is there a benefit to processing multiple OCs per thread (e.g., 2 or 4) to amortize input loads via register reuse?
